authority.legal_name: Ministry of Transport (MOT), State of Qatar
authority.naming_note: Transport split from Communications in 2021; the current ministry is the Ministry of Transport (MOT), mot.gov.qa. Legacy 'MOTC' handle persists on some channels. Use 'Ministry of Transport (MOT)' partner-facing.
authority.geography_type: peninsula on the Gulf (compact east-coast bay + northern coastline)
authority.home_waters_label: Doha Bay and the Qatari east coast

mandate.summary: MOT develops and regulates Qatar's integrated land, sea and air transport. Sea transport master-planning sits squarely in its remit, alongside the Doha Metro, the Lusail Tram, and the national bus network — all coordinated through the Sila integrated public-transport system.
current_priorities: Deliver the Qatar Public Transport Master Plan and the updated 2050 Transport Master Plan
Build and operate the national Water Taxi network (Al Wakrah to Al Khor, 8 stations, 3 lines)
Integrate all modes through the Sila public-transport system
Advance MOT Strategy 2025-2030 and the sustainability goals of Qatar National Vision 2030

policy_targets.ghg_target: 25% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 (Qatar National Environment and Climate Change Strategy)
policy_targets.vision: Qatar National Vision 2030 (QNV2030) — sustainable development and economic diversification; Third National Development Strategy
policy_targets.relevance: A zero-emission marine transport mode contributes directly to the 25%-by-2030 GHG target and to the eco-friendly public-transport goals MOT has stated for the Water Taxi project.

precedent.headline: Qatar has already built the water-transport infrastructure — and is choosing the vessels now.

existing_water_taxi.operator: Ministry of Transport (operator + vessel type selection underway)
existing_water_taxi.name: Qatar Water Taxi project
phase1_assets: Lusail Ferry Terminal (>2,200 sq m; pontoon with electric chargers for ferry recharging; accommodates four 24-m vessels; waiting area, ticketing, retail/offices)
Pearl Ferry Stop (pontoon, ticketing, customer service)
Corniche Ferry Stop (pontoon, ticketing, customer service)
phase3_areas: Old Doha Port to Al Khor (north), passing Lusail City and Simaisma
existing_water_taxi.master_plan: Updated 2050 Transport Master Plan: a national water-taxi network from Al Wakrah to Al Khor across 8 stations on 3 lines, connecting Doha, Lusail, Hamad International Airport, Doha Port, West Bay, The Pearl and Simaisma.
existing_water_taxi.integration: Designed to connect with the Sila public-transit system once operational.
existing_water_taxi.key_fact_for_navier: MOT has built electric-charging pontoons and is STILL selecting the operator and the vessel type. The infrastructure is zero-emission-ready and the boat decision is open — Navier is the natural answer.

qatar_bahrain_ferry.note: First-ever direct international passenger sea route in the Gulf; booking via the Masar app. Makes the Qatar<->Bahrain corridor a live bilateral reality — the precedent for an optional, secondary regional link. Domestic network leads.

metro_tram.relevance: A water layer plugs into an already-built rail and bus network at shared interchanges (Lusail, West Bay/DECC, Old Doha Port) via Sila.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is not introducing a novelty. MOT has already built water-taxi terminals with electric-charging pontoons and published a national network from Al Wakrah to Al Khor. Navier is the vessel choice that makes that network fast and zero-emission from day one: foiling hulls are quicker, near-silent, low-wake, weather-resilient and longer-range than conventional displacement ferries — enough to serve the dense Doha Bay core, the airport and Al Wakrah, the northern coastal extension, and a credible cross-Gulf relief corridor.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real berths/pontoons during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. The first three are the LIVE Phase-1 stations (Lusail, Pearl, Corniche). The rest are published Phase-2/3 stations plus a leisure node.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The dense Doha Bay core: Lusail to the West Bay/Corniche waterfront. One of the two live Phase-1 legs, foiling-upgraded.
Corniche/West Bay to The Pearl — the second live Phase-1 leg; today a congested road loop around the bay.
Closes the inner-bay triangle between the three live stations.
West Bay/Corniche to Old Doha Port (Mina District) — Phase-2 station, events and waterfront.
Waterside airport access from the Doha core, bypassing road congestion at airport peaks. Phase-2.
Doha core to Al Wakrah (southern Phase-2 terminus) along the sheltered east coast.
Old Doha Port to Katara Cultural Village — Phase-2 cultural/tourism node.
Doha core to Banana Island (Anantara) — a live resort water-shuttle corridor today; demonstrates leisure reach.
Northern coastal extension toward Simaisma. Phase-3 line.
Simaisma to Al Khor (northern Phase-3 terminus). Completes the Al Wakrah-to-Al Khor published spine.
Hub-spoke: Old Doha Port (Mina District) ↔ West Bay / DECC waterfront (orphan BP on published network)

regional_links.note: Secondary and clearly optional. One is already a live bilateral reality (the Qatar<->Bahrain ferry). Neither leads the proposal.

links.note: Mirrors the operating Qatar<->Bahrain passenger ferry (Al-Ruwais <-> Sa'ada Marina, Nov 2025). A foiling option on a corridor the two countries already run. Quanta-LR range class.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic and regional leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings. Hand-curated waypoints required where reclamation edges, dredged channels, shipping lanes, reefs or shallows would otherwise be clipped.

hazards.detail: The Pearl, Lusail and West Bay are reclaimed; snap entries to the dredged approach-channel mouths, not the reclaimed edge. The inner bay shoals quickly outside the channels.

hazards.hazard: Hamad Port / Doha commercial shipping channel
hazards.detail: Keep clear of the commercial shipping fairway serving Hamad Port and Doha Port; cross only at marked points. Hamad International Airport sits on reclaimed land — approach via the marked channel.

hazards.hazard: Northern coastal shallows & sandbars (Simaisma, Al Khor)
hazards.detail: The north coast toward Simaisma and Al Khor has extensive shallow flats, sandbars and the Al Khor mangrove/sabkha fringe. Keep geometry in charted deeper water offshore and approach Al Khor via its marked channel.
Banana Island is reef-fringed; snap the approach to the dredged channel, not the reef edge.
The optional Doha<->Bahrain leg crosses open Gulf water with offshore oil/gas fields and shipping lanes; route through charted water clear of platforms and fairways.

sources.what: MOT Water Taxi Phase-1 infrastructure complete (Lusail Terminal + Pearl + Corniche; electric-charging pontoons; Phase-2/3 areas)
Updated 2050 Transport Master Plan water-taxi network (Al Wakrah to Al Khor, 8 stations, 3 lines)

provenance.author: Tasklet
